summary: Abu Hurayra, wiping his nose with a fine cloth, recalls how he once collapsed from extreme hunger by the Prophet's pulpit and was taken for insane.
notes: Text says Ibn Seereen; full name taken from n00364, where he is named Muhammad bin Seereen.

summary: Abu Hurayra recalls serving Uthmaan and Bujra for food and a mount, and his gratitude when Allaah gave him Bujra in marriage.
notes: Three reports in one item: Abu Hurayra's statement, then 'Another narration', then 'Yet another narration' via Saleem bin Hayaan, who quotes his father (unnamed, not tagged). The wife is called Bujra in one report and the daughter of Ghazwaan in another.

summary: Abu Hurayra describes the bare food and clothing of the early days, and Ibn Mas'ood reports the Prophet telling the Sahabah they were better off then than they would be with plenty.
notes: Two reports joined: Abu Hurayra's (with a sub-report 'Another narration') and Ibn Mas'ood's account of the Prophet's words.

summary: Muhammad bin Seereen reports that a Companion would go three days without food, eating toasted leather or binding a stone to his stomach.
Fudhaala bin Ubayd reports that men of Suffa collapsed from hunger during the Prophet's salaah, and the Prophet told them of the reward for their hardship.
Anas reports that seven Companions survived on a single date and fallen leaves until their mouths were sore.
Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet gave seven dates to seven Companions suffering hunger, one for each.
Abu Hurayra reports Companions leaving home in hunger and the Prophet giving them dates, and Aamir recalls a single date shared on an expedition.
notes: Abu Hurayra's report is cut off by footnote and cross-reference text ('Bazzaar as quoted...'). A remark on eight hundred men at the trench comes next, then Aamir's report. Only the first name Aamir is given, so he is not matched to Aamir bin Fuhayra in n00398.

summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah recalls that the Prophet sent a small force under Abu Ubaydah with one bag of dates, given out a single date each.
notes: Ends at 'The Hadith continues.' The reference line listing Maalik, Bukhari, Muslim and Tabraani on the numbers is not tagged.

summary: Jaabir bin Abdillaah tells a student that once the dates ran out they missed even that one date.
notes: Maalik is Imaam Maalik, who relays Jaabir's words. The student is unnamed.

summary: Abu Khunays Ghifaari recounts how, on the Tihaama expedition, the Prophet gathered the Sahabah's leftover provisions at Umar's advice, made du'aa, and every satchel was filled.
Umar recounts how the Prophet blessed a small pile of leftover food on an expedition so that everyone was filled, then taught the Kalimah and its reward.
notes: Some words are garbled by OCR ('Take but do not', 'Rasulullaah them said'); the sense is clear.

summary: Sahl bin Sa'd recalls a woman of his tribe who served the Companions a simple beetroot and barley dish every Friday.
notes: A second report ('Another narration') adds that the meal had no fat or stickiness and that the Sahabah were glad on Fridays. The woman is unnamed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abi Awfa reports that during seven battles with the Prophet they ate locusts.
Abu Barzah reports that on an expedition they ate wheat bread from the enemy's ovens and checked their sides for fat, believing wheat bread made people fat.
An unnamed Companion says that at Khaybar, while with the Prophet, they drove the enemy off the fine wheat bread they had baked.
notes: Narrator unnamed.

summary: Abu Hurayra recounts that after Khaybar they drove Jewish bakers away from their wheat bread and shared it, and he checked his sides for fat.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence ('whether I had become'). OCR has merged the next chapter heading into the end of the text.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports Umar's account of the thirst on the Tabook expedition, and how Abu Bakr asked the Prophet for du'aa and rain then fell.
At Yarmook, three mortally wounded Companions each passed the water to another, and all died before drinking it.
notes: Ikrama bin Abi Jahal is not the approved abu-jahal entry; he is a Companion, not the father.

summary: Muhammad bin Hanafiyyah reports that Abu Amr Ansaari, weak with thirst while fasting, kept firing arrows in Allaah's path after hearing the Prophet's words on their reward, and was martyred before sunset.
notes: A second report ('Another narration') says he asked his slave for water, which the slave gave.

summary: Abu Rayhaana recounts volunteering for a night guard in the cold, when the Prophet made du'aa for him and said the fire of Jahannam is forbidden to the eye that guards in Allaah's path.
notes: The narrator's name is missing from the opening and comes only from the heading. The Ansaari volunteer is unnamed.

summary: Khabbaab bin Arat recounts Hamza's burial, when there was only one small shawl to shroud him.

Shafaa bint Abdillaah reports that she rebuked the Prophet for having nothing to give her, then found her son-in-law Shurahbeel without a decent garment for the Masjid because the Prophet had borrowed his only cloth.
notes: Shafaa's daughter, Shurahbeel's wife, is unnamed.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Jibra'eel asked, through the Prophet, whether Abu Bakr was pleased with Allaah in his poverty, and Abu Bakr affirmed that he was.
notes: Jibra'eel is an angel and is not tagged.

summary: Ali recounts that when he married Faatima, their only bedding was a sheepskin and they had no servant.
Abu Burda relays his father Abu Moosa Ash'ari's account of wearing sheepskin and living on dates and water, so that the Companions smelled like sheep when caught in the rain.
notes: Three versions joined: the first from Abu Burda quoting his father, then 'Another from Abu Burda', then 'Yet another narration' adding the diet. Only the first is clearly from Abu Burda.

summary: Abu Hurayra reports seeing seventy men of Suffa, none with a large shawl, who held their garments together so they would not be exposed.
Waathila bin Asqa says the men of Suffa had no complete clothing, and Aa'isha contrasts her slave-woman's plain shirt with the shirt she once had, which Madinah women borrowed for weddings.
notes: Two reports: Waathila's, then Aa'isha's account of the visitor and the shirt, a separate incident. The visitor and the slave-woman are unnamed.

summary: Hudhayfa recounts a freezing night at the Battle of Ahzaab, when the Prophet sent him to gather news of the enemy, prayed for his protection, and covered him with his shawl on his return.
notes: Hudhayfa has no surname in the text, so he is not matched to any approved entry. Abu Sufyaan is matched to abu-sufyaan.

summary: Yazeed Taymi reports that Hudhayfa, asked by a man who wished he had fought beside the Prophet, described the night of Ahzaab and the shawl the Prophet put over him when he returned cold.
notes: Two reports: the first repeats n00389 in summary, the second ('This narration however') adds the shawl and wake-up details. The man who spoke is unnamed.

summary: The Prophet asks who will go to gather news of the enemy, promising the volunteer companionship in Jannah, but no one stands up from fear, hunger and cold.
notes: Narrator unnamed.

summary: Abu Saa'ib relays a report from a man of Banu Abdul Ash'hal who, wounded at Uhud, marched after the Prophet's caller with his brother, carrying him in turn.
notes: The man and his brother are unnamed here; n00393 names them as Abdullaah and Raafi bin Sahl.

summary: Abdullaah bin Sahl and his brother Raafi bin Sahl went to Hamraa'ul Asad despite their wounds, with no transport, each carrying the other in turn.
notes: Opens with 'Another narration' and has no named narrator. Raafi bin Sahl is not matched to the approved entry raafi, which is an ambiguous name.

summary: Several elders of Banu Salma report that the crippled Amr bin Jamooh asked to march to Uhud, the Prophet excused him from jihaad, yet he went and was martyred.
notes: The narrators are unnamed elders of Banu Salma. Amr bin Jamooh's four sons are unnamed. He is not on the approved list.

summary: Abu Qataadah reports that Amr bin Jamooh asked the Prophet whether he would walk in Jannah with a healthy leg if martyred, and the Prophet said he could see him doing so after his death.
notes: Amr bin Jamooh's nephew and slave are unnamed.

summary: Yahya bin Abdul Hameed reports that Raafi bin Khadeej, struck by an arrow, chose to have only the shaft removed so the Prophet could bear witness to his martyrdom, and that he died later under Mu'aawiya.
notes: Ends with the author's editorial note on his death date (Al Bidaaya, Isaaba) and a cross-reference to the chapter on patience; that part is not narration. The battle is named as Uhud or as a word garbled by OCR. The grandfather Yahya cites is unnamed. Mu'aawiya is taken as Mu'aawiya bin Abi Sufyaan, the Khalifah.

summary: Urwa reports that the Quraysh plotted to seize, kill or exile the Prophet, that Allaah revealed the plan to him, and that he was warned of a plot to kill him in his sleep on the day he went to Abu Bakr's house.
notes: Ends mid-sentence. The text calls him Hadhrat Urwa (RA), but the name matches Urwa bin Zubayr, who is usually counted a Successor, so sahabi is marked unsure.

summary: Ali sleeps in the Prophet's bed while the Prophet and Abu Bakr hide in the cave of Thowr, where Allaah sends tranquillity when the Mushrikeen reach it; Aamir bin Fuhayra and Abdullaah bin Abi Bakr look after them.
notes: The guide is named Ibnul Ayqadh here and Abdullaah bin Urayqidh in n00399; they may be the same man. The Mushrikeen are unnamed.

summary: Aa'isha recounts how the Prophet told Abu Bakr at midday that he was permitted to migrate, Abu Bakr asked to accompany him, and Abu Bakr had camels ready; a second report says the Prophet insisted on buying one.
notes: Two reports: Aa'isha's, then a 'reliable narration' from Aa'isha about buying the camel. The guide may be the Ibnul Ayqadh of n00398.

summary: Asmaa bint Abi Bakr recounts preparing provisions for the Hijrah and tying them with her belt, and how the Prophet and Abu Bakr hid in the cave while the Quraysh searched for them.
notes: This report says they stayed three nights in the cave; n00398 says two days and two nights. The source is inconsistent and has not been corrected.
